subject: Post-call: Lexicor model-fit recommendations + prompt batch intake
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Ari Kaplan <ari@lexicorhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Jul 2028 13:02:00 -0400
Subject: Post-call recap + next steps (model candidates & prompt batch)

Thanks again for your time this morning Ari — good conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned on the evaluation scope and prompt collection: 

Summary of needs
- Primary use case: patient-facing triage assistant + internal summarization for care managers. Sensitive PII/PHI occasionally present in examples.
- Latency target: median < 300ms for 512-token reads; bursty peak traffic during morning hours.
- Quality priorities: hallucination minimization for medication and appointment instructions; conservative answer style for clinical recommendations.

Redwood's initial model recommendations (to evaluate)
- Candidate A: 13B quantized variant — best tradeoff for multi-turn clinical context, better factuality under our benchmarks.
- Candidate B: 7B instruction-tuned, faster and cheaper for non-critical summarization paths.
- Fallback route: smaller 3–4B distilled model for non-sensitive quick lookups (lower cost).

Benchmarks & artifacts
- I attached a short SAQ we ran with Lexicor-like prompts (Lexicor_SAQ_Responses.pdf) and a CSV template for the prompt batch. I'll also drop our internal benchmark link here: https://redwood-inference.internal/reports/benchmarks/lexicor-7-13b-compare

Request: prompt batch + edge cases
- Ask: Could you share ~200–300 representative prompts (CSV is attached template) across the following buckets: patient questions, appointment scheduling, medication clarification, triage escalation scenarios, and anonymized edge cases that previously caused wrong guidance?
- For each prompt row please indicate: expected correct output, whether PHI appears, and any redaction required. If you prefer, drop a sample export from your analytics of top queries and we can map them to the template.

Redaction guidance (quick)
- Please remove or redact full names, MRNs, and SSNs. Dates of service are ok to keep at month-level (e.g., Jul 2028).
- If a prompt contains a verbatim medication name or dosage that you want preserved for clinical fidelity testing, flag it as "keep_medication" in the CSV column.

Next steps & timeline
- Lexicor: provide prompt batch + any compliance SAQ answers by Aug 8.
- Redwood: prepare two model configs and run 1k-prompt dry-run (internal) followed by a seeded 200-prompt evaluation on your sanitized corpus. Target: share initial result deck by Aug 18.

Happy to hop on a quick 20-min call if you want to walk through the CSV template.

Best,
Rachel
Rachel Kim
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
---

On Wed, 25 Jul 2028 at 13:18:42 -0400 Ari Kaplan <ari@lexicorhealth.com> wrote:
> Thanks Rachel — this is exactly the level of detail we needed. A few quick clarifications: 
> 
> 1) Can you confirm whether the 13B quantized candidate will support our VPC private deploy option? We need the model to run inside our VPC for PHI workloads.
> 2) For the CSV template: can we add a column for "business_priority" so our ops team can mark high-impact flows?
> 
> I'll loop in Procurement (copied) for timeline alignment. We should be able to produce an initial 150 prompts by Aug 5 and stretch to 300 by Aug 12.
> 
> —Ari

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Ari Kaplan <ari@lexicorhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Jul 2028 13:26:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + next steps (model candidates & prompt batch)

Thanks Ari — answers below and a small ask for Procurement: 

1) VPC/private deploy: yes — the 13B quantized candidate is compatible with our Private deployment. We'll need to provision a dedicated VPC gateway and a small compute profile for the evaluation (I can draft the checklist for your infra team).

2) CSV: absolutely — adding "business_priority" makes sense. I'll attach an updated template in a follow-up.

Procurement note (to procurement@lexicorhealth.com): procurement, we typically start with an evaluation MSA + a short POC addendum. For accelerated POC customers we can provide a reduced-rate evaluation package. I'll work with Ben to outline pricing and a draft SOW once we confirm the prompt volume and deployment mode.

Rachel

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Ari Kaplan <ari@lexicorhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Jul 2028 13:42:10 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + next steps (model candidates & prompt batch)

Ari — happy to be the procurement touchpoint. Quick pricing note for planning:
- 2-week seeded evaluation (200 prompts) on dedicated 13B-quant infra: estimate $6.5k–8k depending on parallelism and data retention choices.
- If you opt for the 7B path for summarization only, we can run a cheaper concurrent track that cuts token-costs ~40%.

I'll send a short SOW draft and an evaluation quote later today. For the VPC checklist Rachel mentioned, Neha can own the infra onboarding checklist and the KMS/HSM questions.

—Ben

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Ari Kaplan <ari@lexicorhealth.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Jul 2028 14:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + next steps (model candidates & prompt batch)

Ari — sending the VPC onboarding checklist and the minimal KMS metadata we need. Attachment: lexicor_sample_prompts_template.csv (will follow with a version that includes business_priority and keep_medication flags).

Checklist highlights:
- Network: dedicated VPC peering or site-to-site with private subnets and NAT for outbound updates only.
- Keys: KMS ARN and rotation policy; HSM if required per your security team.
- Audit: log sink to your SIEM for token-level eventing during the POC (retention options available).

If you want, we can schedule a 30-min infra handoff to walk your cloud/security folks through the checklist.

Thanks,
Neha

From: Ari Kaplan <ari@lexicorhealth.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Procurement <procurement@lexicorhealth.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Jul 2028 15:10:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + next steps (model candidates & prompt batch)

Appreciate the quick turnaround team. Two quick asks from our side: 
1) Can Redwood provide an example of the regression checks you run (we want to be confident you’ll detect drop in medication accuracy between model versions)?
2) For redaction: please confirm whether Redwood can perform automated redaction suggestions on upload and return a flagged copy for our review before ingestion.

We will aim to provide the first 150 prompts (sanitized) by Aug 5. Procurement will review Ben's draft SOW once received.

—Ari

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Ari Kaplan <ari@lexicorhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Jul 2028 16:28:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + next steps (model candidates & prompt batch)

Great questions — short answers here and I'll follow up with samples: 

1) Regression checks: we run prompt-set anchored regressions — for each model candidate we compare top-line metrics (exact match where applicable, F1 for entity extraction, and a domain-specific medication-fact accuracy score we compute against a curated medication oracle). We also track hallucination rate on the triage prompts and sanity-check token-efficiency. I will attach a redacted sample report from a prior healthcare POC for you to review.

2) Automated redaction suggestions: yes — we can run a pre-ingest redaction pass that flags PHI candidates (names, MRNs, dates, phone numbers). It produces a flagged CSV and a redacted CSV for your review; ingestion does not proceed until you confirm. For anything you want preserved (e.g., medication dosages), use the "keep_medication" flag in the CSV and we will not redact that field.

I'll send the updated CSV template (with business_priority + keep_medication), a short redaction sample, and a previous regression check PDF by end of day. If useful, let's do a 20-min sync with your data ops on Fri at 11am Eastern.

Thanks again — looking forward to the first batch.

Rachel

-----
Attachments: lexicor_sample_prompts_template.csv (template), Lexicor_SAQ_Responses.pdf (SAQ sample)
